subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 4: New Beginnings: Cities and States
central_question: How did renewed urbanisation, larger states, new political systems, technology, trade and social organisation transform India in the first millennium BCE?
in_scope_units: From First to Second Urbanisation—Harappan decline and renewed cities.
Sources—archaeology and late Vedic, Buddhist and Jain literature.
Janapadas and Mahajanapadas—clan territories, rajas, trade and larger states.
Early Democratic Traditions—sabha, samiti, monarchies, ganas and sanghas.
More Innovations—iron, agriculture, warfare, alliances and punch-marked coins.
The Varna–Jati System—occupations, four varnas, flexibility, inequality and later rigidity.
Developments Elsewhere—Uttarapatha, Dakshinapatha, Shishupalgarh, southern kingdoms and overseas trade.
Questions and activities 1–4—Kautilya, ruler selection, sources and iron.

known_pitfalls.claim: Second Urbanisation was an uninterrupted continuation of Harappan cities.
known_pitfalls.correction: It was a new phase after a long decline of Harappan urban life.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every mahajanapada was a hereditary monarchy.
known_pitfalls.correction: Vajji and Malla were gana–sangha systems with powerful assemblies.

known_pitfalls.claim: Iron appeared only after cities grew.
known_pitfalls.correction: Widespread iron tools supported agriculture and state growth.
Jati referred to occupational communities; varna was a four-part Vedic category.

known_pitfalls.claim: The varna–jati system was always equally rigid.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter notes early flexibility and later rigidity.

recommended_example_progression: Use Questions and activities Q1 to interpret Kautilya’s ideal kingdom.
Use Q2 to discuss ruler selection.
Use Q3 to compare archaeological and literary sources.
Use Q4 to explain iron and urbanism.
Use the First/Second Urbanisation table to compare the two phases.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Questions and activities 1–4.
